doc.title: Peter Appleyard interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, October 4, 2012

title: Dinner at the Century Club with Benny Goodman
summary: Goodman took him to the Century Club, ordered expensive wine, and bought tobacco for him.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: paying Zoot Sims.” I said, “Good.” It was a hundred dollars more. So then he said, “Let’s go out to eat and celebrate.” So he took me to, I think it’s called the Century Club. It’s on Fifth Avenue. And the list of members is like John B. Mellon, George D. Rockefeller, blah-blah, Benny Goodman. So we get there and oh it’s incredible. He said, “Do you like it?” I said, “Oh, Benny, it’s just incredible.” It’s all beautiful paneled you know. He said, “It’s like a movie, isn’t it?” I said, “Yeah.” So the waiter came and said, “Mr. Goodman, what would you like tonight?” “Well,” he said, “the roast beef, do you like roast beef, Peter?” I said, “Yeah, I do.” He said, “Well we had that roast beef last time, prime rib. Do you have some?” He said, “Whoa, do we have some tonight, really, Black Angus.” “Good. And by the way, that wine that we had the last time, what was it?” And this was ’72 or ’73. He said, “Yes, Mr. Goodman, it was a Chateau Latour. I think it was ’60.” He said, “bring a bottle of that.” I looked at the menu, it was like five hundred dollars for the bottle. I felt like saying “Benny, I want that money.”
Right. I’ll take that in my salary.
Anyway, he took me downstairs when we were leaving, and I smoked a pipe in those days, and he stopped and said, “Just a minute.” He said, “Give me some tobacco please. Dunhill, for Mr. Appleyard.”
